questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

Don’t use those pencils; __use the one __we bought in Portugal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **use the ones.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, **'ones' **refer to **'pencils'** which is plural, therefore we will use it as it is also plural.
 
• A pronoun must agree with its antecedent (the noun to which it refers) in both number and gender.
 
• We use 'one' and 'ones' -
 
 
• after an adjective__:
 __
 
• Example: *Which is your car, the red **one **or the black one? *(here, one refers to 'car')
 
 
 
• after 'the'__:
 
 
• Example: *Let us look at the photographs - the **ones** you took in Delhi. *(here, ones refers to 'photographs')
 
 
 
• after which in questions:
 
 
• Example: *You can have one toy. Which **one** do you want?* (here, one refers to 'toy')
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate substitute is **'use the ones'**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

The prince __was told kill the dragon__, but in order to do so, he had to cross the Forbidden Mountain.

options.text: was told too kill the dragon
was told to kill the dragon

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **was told to kill the dragon.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, we need a* to-infinitive* **'to kill'** after **'told'.**
 
• ** **Infinitives are the base form of a verb usually used in conjugation with 'to'.__
 __
 
• I want to watch a movie. (Here, 'to watch' __is a to-infinitive and__ 'want'__ is the main verb of the sentence.)
 
 
 
• The to-infinitives are often used to express the purpose of something or someone's opinion about something. 
 __
 
• I have come here to meet__ you. (the to-infinitive** **__'to meet'__ expresses the purpose of the action of coming there)
 
 
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate substitution is **'was told to kill the dragon'.**

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

__
 
• When infinitives occur without 'to', they are called bare infinitives or simply infinitives without to.
 
• Bare infinitives are used after modal verbs.
 
 
• I should go__ there myself. 
 
 
 
• Bare infinitives are also used after some verbs like 'let', 'make', etc.
 __
 
• He made me work__ for him.

questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. **

He cannot speak Spanish because he was born and brought up in Spain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **because he was. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the usage of the conjunction **'because'. **
 
• We use because to mean **'for the reason that; since.'**
 
• In the first clause of the given sentence, it is mentioned that the person cannot speak Spanish.
 
• Now, the clause after 'because' should give us the reason why he cannot speak Spanish.
 
• However, the fact that he was born and brought up in Spain cannot be the reason behind his inability to speak Spanish.
 
• The sentence intends to mean that he cannot speak Spanish** in spite of the fact** that he was born in Spain.
 
• **Hence, the correct sentence will be** - *He cannot speak Spanish **although** he was born and brought up in Spain. *

*​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

__
 
• We can also use 'even though', 'despite the fact that' and 'though'. __
 
• They essentially mean the same thing.

questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. **

Ten years since Mohit left India and started working for the betterment of the downtrodden people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Ten years since.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, the sentence is incomplete as we don't have a subject and a verb for the object 'ten years'.
 
• Also, the use of **'since'** shows that the first part of the sentence is in the Perfect Tense__.
 
• The present perfect shows that the action of leaving India and starting working for the betterment of the downtrodden people started in the past ten years ago and since the person is still outside India and working on the same thing, the action is still going on.
 
• So, we need to add** 'It has been'** before **'ten years'** to make the sentence complete and grammatically correct. 
 
• In 'it has been', 'it' is the subject, 'has' is the auxiliary (helping) verb and 'been' is the main verb. (been is the past participle (third form of the verb) of 'to-be'.
 
• **Therefore, the complete sentence will be **-*** It has been** ten years since Mohit left India and started working for the betterment of the downtrodden people. *

*​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• It is incorrect to say:
 
 
• I know him for ten years.
 
 
 
• The correct way to say this is:
 
 
• I have known him for ten years. [Sub + has\have + the past participle (V3)]

questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. **

If I am a bird, I would fly and explore the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** If I am.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the usage of **'am'**. 
 
• The sentence is an example of *type 2 conditional sentence.*
 
• The second conditional is used to talk about hypothetical situations. 
 
 
• If I were__ a millionaire, I __would__ buy a Ferrari. 
 
• If I __worked __hard, __would__ I pass the exam?
 
 
 
• ​Therefore, we will use the past subjunctive **'were' i**nstead of **'am'**.
 
• We use the past and past perfect subjunctive mood to express necessity, unreality, wishes or hopes.
 __
 
• I wish I were__ a millionaire.
 
• I wish I __hadn't __called her. 
 
 
 
• **Hence, the correct sentence is **- *If I **were** a bird, I would fly and explore the world.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. **

Let us go for a picnic today. The _________ is very pleasant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **weather. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us look at the meanings of the given words:
 
 
• **Atmosphere -** The envelope of gases surrounding the earth or another planet. 
 
• **Climate -** The weather conditions prevailing in an area in general or over a long period.
 
• **Weather - The state of the atmosphere at a place and time as regards heat, dryness, sunshine, wind, rain, etc.**
 
• **Season - **Each of the four divisions of the year (spring, summer, autumn, and winter) marked by particular weather patterns and daylight hours, resulting from the earth's changing position with regard to the sun.
 
 
 
• The decision to go for a picnic depends on whether the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time is pleasant or not.
 
• It may be unpleasant somewhere else but it should be pleasant at the place where we intend to go at the time when we intend to go.
 
• Also, it doesn't have to be pleasant for a long period of time. It can just be pleasant for an hour or a day. 
 
• Therefore,** 'weather'** is the correct word to fill in the blank.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Whether and weather are two different terms.
 
 
• Whether is a conjunction which is used to express a doubt or choice between alternatives.
 
• Example: I wonder whether he will come to the party.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. **

The film we saw last night was boring. I wish I ______ seen it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **hadn't. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• We use** wish + ****past perfect subjunctive** to express unreal past situations - when we need to express that we want a situation in the past to be different.** **
 
• In the first sentence, it is given that the person watched a boring film the previous night.
 
• In the second sentence, the words **'wish'** and** 'seen'** show that he\she regrets having watched it since the film was boring.
 
• Therefore, we will use the past perfect subjunctive **'hadn't'** here.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **Alternate Method__**

__
 
• We can also use the elimination method here.
 
 
• **Didn't **cannot be used here as the verb following the blank is not in the base form.
 
• **Shouldn't **cannot be used here as the verb following the blank needs to be a bare infinitive (the base form of the verb).
 
• We use** 'would\would not have' **with 'if clause' __in *type 3 conditional* sentences. So, it cannot be used here.
 __
 
• If it had rained, you would have gotten wet.
 
• If I had known that this film was boring, I wouldn't have seen it. 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• We use the past and past perfect subjunctive mood to express necessity, unreality, wishes or hopes.
 
 
• I wish I were a millionaire.
 
• I wish I hadn't called her.
